questions: Did the unsteadiness and jerky movements begin suddenly, within minutes or hours?
Have the symptoms been steadily worsening since they began?
Have you had weakness, numbness, facial drooping, or difficulty speaking?
Have you had severe headache, repeated vomiting, double vision, or new visual loss?
Have you experienced vertigo, with the room spinning?
Have you had confusion, fainting, loss of consciousness, or seizures?
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed the dose of any medication?
Have you taken sedatives, anticonvulsants, antipsychotics, recreational drugs, or excessive alcohol recently?
Do the jerky movements occur throughout the body, including when you are at rest?
Have you had fever, a recent infection, or a recent vaccination?
Have you had diarrhea or another significant illness in the weeks before this began?
Have you had difficulty swallowing, slurred speech, or abnormal eye movements?
Have you noticed memory loss, personality change, hallucinations, or other cognitive problems?
Have you had unexplained weight loss, night sweats, or a known cancer?
Have you ever had liver disease, thyroid disease, vitamin deficiency, or exposure to heavy metals?
Have you had similar symptoms previously that came and went?
Does anyone in your family have gait problems, tremor, involuntary movements, or an inherited neurological disorder?
Have you had episodes of painful muscle spasms or sustained abnormal postures?
Have you had recent head injury?
Have you had difficulty controlling your bladder or bowel movements?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Postinfectious autoimmune myoclonus–ataxia syndrome, most likely triggered by recent gastroenteritis (probable Campylobacter-associated), with subcortical myoclonus

Alternative 1: Postinfectious autoimmune cerebellitis

Alternative 2: Seronegative autoimmune cerebellar ataxia, including anti-GAD65 or anti-mGluR1 disease

Alternative 3: Functional movement disorder with functional myoclonus and ataxia
